rea.name: Reverse Engineer Anything
rea.body:
Here's the real Reverse Engineer Anything repo 👇
https://github.com/morluto/rea

Only use this one. Fake copies with malware are going around. Only use it on apps you own or are allowed to inspect.

The prompt I used:
I want to understand one feature of [APP], then build my own version.
1. Use REA to inspect how [FEATURE] works. Start from what the app does on screen, and only go deeper if you need to.
2. Write down what you found in plain English: what triggers it, what data it uses, and what it shows.
3. Build the smallest version of just that feature in [LANGUAGE]. Nothing else from the app.
4. Test yours against the real one side by side and list every difference.
5. Fix the differences and repeat until they match.
Ask me before you install anything or change anything outside this folder.

tv-safe-guide.name: safe TV cleanup guide
tv-safe-guide.body:
Here's the safe step by step guide 👇

Google TV, Android TV or Fire TV: turn on debug mode on your TV, open Claude Code on a laptop on the same WiFi, and paste this prompt:

"Find my TV on this network, connect to it, list every app on it, and tell me which ones are safe to turn off. Don't touch anything until I say yes."

Two rules so you don't break your TV:
1. Tell it to turn apps off, never delete them.
2. Make it save a list of every app first, so you can undo anything.

Samsung, LG, Roku or Vizio? You can't do the AI part, but you can turn off the setting that tracks what you watch. Menu names can vary by model:
Samsung: Settings > Support > Terms & Privacy > Privacy Choices > Viewing Information Services OFF
LG: Settings > General > System > Additional Settings > Live Plus OFF
Roku: Settings > Privacy > Smart TV Experience > Use info from TV inputs OFF
Vizio: System > Reset & Admin > Viewing Data OFF
Sony (Google TV): Settings > Privacy > Samba Interactive TV OFF

More free ones here: https://humzabuilds.github.io

tv-debloat.name: Smart TV cleanup steps
tv-debloat.body:
Here's the safe way, no coding 👇 Do these in order and stop when it's good enough.

1. Turn off what the TV lets you (2 min)
Fire TV: Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings > turn off Interest based Ads, Device Usage Data and Collect App Usage Data
Google TV: Settings > Privacy > Ads > Delete advertising ID
Any TV: in Privacy or Terms, turn off anything about viewing information or content recognition

2. Get a cleaner home screen (10 min, Google TV or Android TV)
Install Projectivy Launcher from the Play Store on your TV. It hides the ad rows, your apps stay, and uninstalling it undoes everything.

I'm not telling you to let an AI delete system apps. That's how someone bricked their TV. Menu names change by model, so if yours looks different, ask any AI: "My TV is a [BRAND] [MODEL]. Where is the privacy and ads menu?"

More free ones here: https://humzabuilds.github.io

tv-privacy.name: TV privacy steps
tv-privacy.body:
Here's where the viewing data setting hides 👇 Names change by model and year, so if yours looks different, paste this into any AI:

My TV is a [BRAND] [MODEL]. Walk me through turning off viewing data / ACR, one menu at a time. Tell me what each menu is called on my exact model.

Samsung: Settings > Support (or General & Privacy) > Terms & Privacy > Privacy Choices > Viewing Information Services: off
LG: Settings > All Settings > General > System > Additional Settings > Live Plus: off
Roku: Settings > Privacy > Smart TV Experience > uncheck Use info from TV inputs
Vizio: Settings > Admin & Privacy > Viewing Data: off
Sony: Settings > look for Samba Interactive TV and turn it off
Hisense / TCL: if it runs Roku or Google TV, follow that menu; otherwise use the prompt

Your apps keep working after. And if you tried my last TV video, turn network debugging back off.

More free ones here: https://humzabuilds.github.io

ai-phone.name: AI phone setup
ai-phone.body:
Here's the setup and my 5 prompts 👇

It's Google's open source Artemis: https://github.com/google/artemis

Setup: plug an Android phone into your laptop, turn on USB debugging, then run this one line:
git clone https://github.com/google/artemis.git && cd artemis && ./start.sh
It connects itself to Claude Code.

My first 5 prompts:
1) Find the cheapest ride home and show me before you book.
2) Turn off every notification except texts and calls.
3) Clear every unread badge and tell me what you skipped.
4) Find my last 3 food orders and tell me what I spent.
5) Set my phone up for sleep: Do Not Disturb at 11, alarm at 7.
Always end with: show me before you buy, book or send anything.

Before you try it: your AI can see everything on your screen, so use a spare phone, or log out of your bank and email first. Android only for now; iPhone is on their roadmap.

ai-jarvis.name: Build your own Jarvis
ai-jarvis.body:
Here are the 4 pieces and a build prompt 👇

1) Ears: Whisper (free, runs on your computer): pip install -U openai-whisper (also needs ffmpeg)
2) Eyes: Google's MediaPipe Gesture Recognizer. It tracks your hand through the webcam and knows a closed fist or a finger pointing up out of the box.
3) Brain: Claude Code in headless mode: claude -p "your words" --allowedTools "Read,Write,Bash(open *)" (without it, headless mode refuses tools that need approval). Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless
4) Mouth: Kokoro, a free open voice model: pip install kokoro soundfile

Paste this into Claude Code:
"Build me a voice assistant on this computer. Listen with Whisper, watch my webcam with MediaPipe's gesture recognizer (closed fist = start dictation), send what I say to claude -p, and speak the answer with Kokoro. Add one hotkey that stops everything."

Safety: keep the camera and mic on your own computer, only allow the tools it needs with --allowedTools, and make it ask you before it sends, buys or deletes anything.

yt-agent.name: AI agent that watches YouTube for you
yt-agent.body:
Here are the 4 commands and a build prompt 👇

1) List the newest videos with yt-dlp (free, open source): yt-dlp --flat-playlist -I 1:10 --print "%(id)s %(title)s" "https://www.youtube.com/@CHANNEL/shorts" Docs: https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp
2) Grab only the audio: yt-dlp -f "ba[ext=m4a]" -o "%(id)s.%(ext)s" VIDEO_URL
3) Write down every word with Whisper (free, runs on your computer): pip install -U openai-whisper (also needs ffmpeg), then whisper VIDEO_ID.m4a --model small --output_format txt
4) Pull out the hooks with Claude Code in headless mode: cat *.txt | claude -p "Give me the first sentence of each transcript and the hook patterns that repeat" --tools ""

Paste this into Claude Code:
"Build me a daily script on this computer. Take my list of YouTube channels, use yt-dlp to list each one's 10 newest Shorts, download only the audio, transcribe it with Whisper, then pipe the transcripts to claude -p with all tools turned off and write me a one page report of the hook patterns that repeat. Run it once a day."

Safety: use it for your own notes on public videos. Never re-upload anyone's video or copy their script word for word, and run claude -p with --tools "" so it has no tools at all and only reads the text you pipe in.

safe-cleanup.name: safe storage cleanup prompt
safe-cleanup.body:
Here's the safe storage cleanup prompt 👇

Paste this into Claude Code in your home folder:

"Find the 20 biggest folders and files in my home folder. Use only names, sizes and dates; do not open or read any file. Do not delete, move or change anything yet. Mark anything in iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Photos, Mail, Messages, Library or AppData as DO NOT TOUCH. For each item, tell me what it is, whether it is safe to remove, and how much space I would get back. Then wait for me to pick. Show me the exact path and wait for my yes before each move. Move items only to the Trash (Mac) or Recycle Bin (Windows); never use rm, del or Remove-Item, never empty the Trash, and if a move fails, tell me and stop."

Before you run it:
1. Back up first: Time Machine on Mac, File History on Windows.
2. Keep Claude Code in manual mode so it asks before it changes anything (Shift+Tab cycles the modes, so check which one is on).
3. Trash or Recycle Bin only, and don't empty it until you've checked. Put Back undoes a move.
4. Never move synced folders (iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Photos): trashing one deletes it on every device.

More free ones here: https://humzabuilds.github.io

scan-to-text.name: Unlimited OCR 2 setup prompt
scan-to-text.body:
Here's Unlimited OCR 2 👇
https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR

Setup prompt (paste into Claude Code or your own AI coding agent):

"Set up Unlimited OCR 2 from github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR on this computer. Read the README first and follow its install steps. Before you run anything, show me every command and every file you will download, and wait for my yes. Use a new Python environment so nothing else on my computer changes. Then run it on one PDF I pick and save the text next to it."

Before you run it:
1. You need an NVIDIA graphics card. Baidu tested it on an NVIDIA A800-80GB, so smaller cards may be slow or run out of memory.
2. It loads with trust_remote_code=True, so read the code before you run it.
3. Skip the online demo for anything private. Run it on your own machine so your files never leave your computer.

room.name: read-only hotel room check prompt
room.body:
Here's my read-only version of the prompt 👇 Paste it into Claude Code on the Wi-Fi the room gave you:

"You are a read-only check-in safety assistant on the Wi-Fi this room gave me. Explain each command in one line and ask before running it. 1) List devices on this network (arp-scan or nmap -sn only, no port attacks, no logins, never open a video stream). Show device names and MAC addresses masked unless the vendor is a camera maker, and flag any camera brands. 2) Run a 30 second Bluetooth scan every 2 minutes for 10 minutes and flag AirTag, Tile or SmartTag signals. 3) Walk me through a flashlight sweep of mirrors, vents and anything pointed at the bed or shower. 4) Give me a ranked table and next steps. Remind me a clean result is not proof."

Good to know:
1. Some hotels ban network scans in their Wi-Fi rules. If you're unsure, or staff object, skip step 1 and do the Bluetooth and flashlight checks.
2. A clean result isn't proof. Still check the room with your own eyes.

More free ones here: https://humzabuilds.github.io
